evidence.quote: To fit the non-parametric source, we first fix the parameters of the lens object according to our parametric mass model (see Sect. 3.2.2), and then use a pixelized Voronoi grid that adapts to the mass model’s magnification pattern, giving higher resolutions to areas with higher magnification.

findings_qualitative.value: A well-separated, kpc-scaled, single-sided radio jet is located at a projected distance of ~1.15-1.2 kpc to the northwest of the Cloverleaf host galaxy in the reconstructed source plane.

evidence.quote: With both parametric and non-parametric lens models and with reconstructed images in the source plane, we find a well-separated, kpc-scaled, single-sided radio jet located at projected ~1.2 kpc to the northwest of the host galaxy in the source plane.

evidence.loc: 4.2 The discovery of a radio jet
evidence.quote: All reconstructed radio images show extended emission to the northwest of the dust continuum core, at a projected distance of ~1.15 kpc (0.14'') away from the centre of the host galaxy.

findings_qualitative.value: The radio jet exhibits a steep power-law spectral index (~1.11) dominated by synchrotron emission, whereas the host galaxy exhibits a flatter spectral index (~0.70-0.80) likely combining free-free, dust continuum, and supernova-remnant synchrotron emission.

evidence.loc: 5.4 The Power-Law Profiles of the SEDs
evidence.quote: As shown in Fig. 3 and Table 5, the SEDs of the radio jet in both lens plane and source plane exhibit power-law profiles, and have similar spectral indices, which indicates that the emission is dominated by the synchrotron from electrons in the jet material.

evidence.loc: 5.4 The Power-Law Profiles of the SEDs
evidence.quote: On the position of the host galaxy, the SED can be also fitted with one single power-law profile with a flatter spectral index (see Fig. 5 and Table 5) compared with the one at the position of the radio jet.

findings_qualitative.value: The co-existence of broad absorption line winds and the newly discovered radio jet suggests AGN feedback in the Cloverleaf quasar operates via both radiation-driven wind and kinetic jet modes.

evidence.quote: together with the broad absorption line and the newly discovered radio jet, we suggest that the AGN feedback in Cloverleaf consists of coexistent contributions from both radiation-driven wind and AGN-launched jet.

claims.hypothesis: High-resolution multi-wavelength lens reconstructions of the Cloverleaf quasar can spatially separate emission from the central AGN, the dusty host galaxy, and any radio jet structures.
claims.experiment: Reconstructed the source plane of Cloverleaf using parametric and non-parametric (Voronoi mesh) lens models in PyAutoLens across HST F814W, ALMA 300 GHz, e-Merlin 1.5 GHz, and VLA 8.4 and 33 GHz images.
claims.result: The 300 GHz continuum reconstructs as an extended disk-like host galaxy of 0.115'' x 0.109'' FWHM, while all three radio bands reveal an extended radio clump of ~0.9-1.2 kpc located ~1.15 kpc (0.14'') to the northwest of the host galaxy centre on the inner caustics.
claims.finding: Cloverleaf hosts a well-separated, kpc-scaled, single-sided radio jet to the northwest of its host galaxy.

evidence.quote: With both parametric and non-parametric lens models and with reconstructed images in the source plane, we find a well-separated, kpc-scaled, single-sided radio jet located at projected ~1.2 kpc to the northwest of the host galaxy in the source plane.

evidence.loc: 4.2 The discovery of a radio jet
evidence.quote: All reconstructed radio images show extended emission to the northwest of the dust continuum core, at a projected distance of ~1.15 kpc (0.14'') away from the centre of the host galaxy.

claims.hypothesis: The radio emission in the northwest clump and in the host galaxy arise from distinct physical mechanisms.
claims.experiment: Measured multi-frequency radio fluxes (1.5, 8.4, and 33 GHz) in both the lens and source planes and fitted power-law spectral indices and pixel-by-pixel spectral index maps.
claims.result: The radio jet has a steep power-law spectral index (\alpha_fitted = 1.11 \pm 0.04 in the source plane, 1.11 \pm 0.01 in the lens plane), whereas the host galaxy has a flatter spectral index (\alpha_fitted = 0.70 \pm 0.06 in the source plane, 0.80 \pm 0.02 in the lens plane).
claims.finding: The radio jet emission is dominated by synchrotron radiation from jet electrons, while the host galaxy radio emission has flatter-spectrum contributions from free-free/dust continuum and supernova remnants.

evidence.quote: As shown in Fig. 3 and Table 5, the SEDs of the radio jet in both lens plane and source plane exhibit power-law profiles, and have similar spectral indices, which indicates that the emission is dominated by the synchrotron from electrons in the jet material.

claims.hypothesis: AGN feedback in the Cloverleaf quasar operates via both radiative wind (quasar mode) and kinetic jet (radio mode) mechanisms simultaneously.
claims.experiment: Combined the discovery of the kpc-scale radio jet with known optical broad absorption line profiles and X-ray/IR constraints on the AGN Eddington ratio from literature.
claims.result: The ~1.15 kpc radio jet co-exists with high-velocity broad absorption line winds and an active quasar radiating at an Eddington ratio of ~0.1.
claims.finding: AGN feedback in the Cloverleaf quasar likely involves co-existent contributions from both radiation-driven winds and an AGN-launched radio jet.

evidence.quote: together with the broad absorption line and the newly discovered radio jet, we suggest that the AGN feedback in Cloverleaf consists of coexistent contributions from both radiation-driven wind and AGN-launched jet.
The co-existence of a radio jet and broad absorption line indicates that the Cloverleaf quasar likely feedbacks its host galaxy with both AGN wind and radio jet.

why_this_data.value: Optical (HST) traces point-like QSO emission, sub-millimetre (ALMA 300 GHz) resolves the extended dusty host galaxy disk free of microlensing to tightly constrain the lens mass model, and multi-band radio (e-Merlin and VLA) traces synchrotron emission from relativistic particles in the jet.

evidence.quote: This work focuses on observational data at three wavelengths: (i) optical, which is dominated by the QSO emission and is seen as almost four point sources from HST images (Kneib et al. 1998); (ii) Sub-millimetre, which traces the gaseous dusty disk of the host galaxy
The extended lensed arc at the submillimeter wavelength is not subject to the micro-lensing effect and its entire brightness distribution can be used to improve the precision of the lens model.

why_this_method.value: Non-parametric Voronoi mesh modelling adapts resolution to source morphology and magnification, overcoming parametric limitations for irregular sources; using a magnification-weighted mesh with a fixed ALMA-derived mass model produces identical Voronoi cells across radio bands for pixel-by-pixel spectral index mapping.

evidence.quote: The traditional method (e.g. Kneib et al. 1998), which is based on parametric modelling, has limitations in the cases of irregular sources. The newly developed non-parametric modelling, which is required for high angular resolution and high sensitivity analysis, greatly improves the reconstructed source plane

This is because a magnification-based mesh produces an identical grid of Voronoi cells across all three frequency channels, ensuring consistent sampling of the source when calculating the spectral indices pixel by pixel to obtain a spectral indices map.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Rejected the possibility that the radio jet feature originates from the foreground lens galaxy rather than the background lensed quasar, because multiple components appear across all radio bands and their merging morphology between components B and D matches a background source lying on the inner caustics.

evidence.loc: 5.2 Possibility to be a jet in the foreground?
evidence.quote: One may also ask if the radio feature comes from the foreground lens galaxy, instead of the background source galaxy. First, the multiple components shown in all radio bands indicate that it is unlikely to be multiple jets from the centre.

evidence.loc: 5.2 Possibility to be a jet in the foreground?
evidence.quote: Second, the spatial distributions of all radio components are highly consistent with the scenario that the radio structure locates on the caustics, i.e. merging between lensed components (Appendix A).

limitations_admitted.value: Three of the 18 VLA 33 GHz execution blocks taken before 22 Oct. 2013 were corrupted and unusable due to incomplete execution.

evidence.quote: However, three of them, taken before 22 Oct. 2013, were corrupted and not usable due to incomplete execution.

limitations_admitted.value: The four optical point-source images may suffer from microlensing, which is not included in the strong lens modelling, and provide limited constraints on the lens model.

evidence.quote: The four optical images of Cloverleaf point sources may suffer from micro-lensing (Kayser et al. 1990), which may lead to a biased result since the micro-lensing effect is not included in the strong lens modelling.

limitations_admitted.value: Several reconstructed 300 GHz emission clumps outside the caustics have lower fidelity due to lens model uncertainty.

evidence.loc: 4.2 The discovery of a radio jet
evidence.quote: Due to the uncertainty of the lens model, several emission clumps outside the caustics have less fidelity.

limitations_admitted.value: A counter-jet on the opposite side of the host galaxy may be too faint to detect with current sensitivity if it lies away from the caustics.

evidence.quote: Depending on the geometry, the other side of the radio jet might be too faint to be detected due to being away from the caustics, or simply does not exist.

limitations_admitted.value: A numerical plotting issue caused the inner critical curve in Figures A1 and B1 to be drawn as an ellipse rather than a point.

evidence.quote: The solid black line and the red solid line are the outer and the inner critical curve (which is incorrect due to the numerical issue and should be a point) in the lens plane respectively.

referee_caveats_inferred: Astrometric alignment relies on shifting the HST image to match the ALMA continuum peaks, assuming the optical AGN and sub-mm dust continuum peaks are spatially coincident, which may introduce small systematic offsets in the fixed lens centre.
Lens modelling appears to be performed on cleaned images with correlated noise rather than directly in the interferometric uv-plane.

data_public_as_stated.value: All observational data are publicly available in the HST, ALMA, VLA, and e-Merlin archives.

evidence.quote: All data adopted in this work are publicly available in corresponding data archival systems of HST, ALMA, VLA, and e-Merlin.
